summary: Space Base Odyssey is a cooperative Roblox game where kids aged 7 to 12 land at the Moon's south pole and grow a base from nothing. They carry parts from their lander and build the habitat, solar panels, a greenhouse, an antenna, a regolith storm shelter, a lab, ice drills, vehicles and finally a ship for Mars. An open world with 21 main quests and 9 side quests teaches one system at a time, and missions ask crews to share limited power between air, food and science every morning: every choice costs something. Solar storms replay real flares from NASA's DONKI database, live or archived and always labelled honestly, including real false alarms. 13 learning achievements reward what kids understand, the game runs in English and Spanish, and nobody ever gets hurt: a mission that goes wrong ends safely with a report that explains why.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Space Base Odyssey is a 3D outpost trainer built in Roblox Studio for kids aged 7 to 12. Players start in the lander that brought them to the Moon's south pole, near the rim of Shackleton crater, and build a base step by step with C.A.R.L., a tracked helper robot that guides them and rescues anyone whose suit runs out of air. Every sentence has at most eight simple words, in English or Mexican Spanish.

Play it on Roblox: https://www.roblox.com/games/98598885274802

HOW IT ANSWERS THE CHALLENGE

- Power budgeting: each morning players share power cells (one per clean solar array plus a battery) between life support, greenhouse and science. A cell for science is a cell taken from air or food; dust takes a cell away until someone cleans the panel.

- Life support: oxygen is made from water with electricity. Players fetch ice from a dark crater, fix leaks and refill suits; breathing, leaks and refills use air.

- Food production: today's greenhouse power is tomorrow's food. Plants take time.

- Radiation shielding: during a solar storm players run to a thick regolith shelter. Dose received outside rises live and never goes down; the shelter protects by mass, not power.

- Communication delay: aligning the antenna with Earth gives a 45-second storm warning instead of 15 and sends science data home (signals take about 1.3 s from the Moon, 3 to 22 minutes from Mars).

HOW IT PLAYS

An open world with 21 main quests and 9 side quests teaches one system at a time, and the habitat grows through five base levels, from landing camp to spaceport. Training and story missions have a calm planning phase and a 150-second work shift, then a day-by-day report explains every result. 13 learning achievements unlock only when the server sees the real event and say what the kid learned. Three save slots per player save automatically; each world runs in its own private server, alone or with up to 3 Roblox friends.

REAL NASA DATA, HONESTLY LABELLED

At server start the game asks NASA / CCMC DONKI for the solar flares and particle events of the last 30 days. Strong live flares are replayed as storms and labelled live with their date; otherwise an archive of 11 real X-class flares is used and labelled as a replay. Some are real false alarms (the X9.0 flare of October 2024 brought no particle storm), teaching that a big flare does not always mean danger. The game always asks "what if a storm like this reached your base?" and never presents archived data as live.

HOW IT WORKS

Roblox Studio and Luau, synced from the repository with Rojo; the world is built by code. The server is authoritative and validates every player action. Every number lives in shared modules, tagged REAL (with its source in DATA_SOURCES.md) or GAME (chosen for playability). Automated tests run with Lune (over 43,000 checks, including every text in English and Spanish); the balance test proves that no fixed power plan earns 3 stars without reacting to events.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Kids feel trade-offs (the food meter drops the day after they cut the greenhouse), learn real science told simply, work as a team, fail safely with an explanation, and see the real date of every replayed flare. It fits a 15-minute class or hours of play at home.

TOOLS

Roblox Studio, Luau, Rojo, Lune, Git/GitHub, HyperFrames (video editing), Tabler Icons (MIT), and Claude by Anthropic as an AI assistant.

SI DISCLOSURE

Claude (Anthropic) assisted with research and fact checking, code and tests, text drafts and translations, and video editing; the team made every design decision and reviewed all numbers and texts. Every AI-assisted code file starts with a disclosure line. The demo video uses real in-game footage; its voiceover was generated with AI (ElevenLabs) from a script written by the team; the music was synthesized in code; sound effects come from Freesound via Openverse (CC BY / CC0). The game itself contains no AI-generated images, video or audio.
